q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of a pedestal fan?
title: Pedestal fan carbon footprint per fan
short: Weigh the motor, blades, guard, stand and base per fan and multiply by supplier figures. Add winding, moulding, painting and assembly energy, then divide the plant's energy by fans made.

ul: Motor with copper or aluminium winding.
Plastic or metal blades and steel guard.
Steel stand and plastic or metal base.
Moulding blades and parts, and painting metal parts.

p: Report per fan by sweep and weight. Use-phase electricity is usually far larger than the factory figure, so give the rated wattage too.

example.title: Worked example: plant energy per fan (one month)
lines: Plant total: 28,400 / 20,000 = 1.420 kg CO2 per fan
Add motor, blades and stand for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
